episodes.207510: A line of showers and thunderstorms moved across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening of November 7, 2025. With warm, moist air ahead of a cold front along with abundant wind shear, this environment allowed for damaging wind gusts along the leading edge of the thunderstorms. Several reports of downed trees were received along with a few reports of hail up the size of quarters. With waning instability, these thunderstorms weakened as they got east of Nashville and closer to the Cumberland Plateau.
episodes.208497: Several rare November supercells developed across South Carolina as a deep mid and upper level trough pushed across the southeast US. This trough interacted with anomalously high instability and a steep moisture gradient that helped enhance the wind fields to favor supercellular convection. Each of these supercells produced large hail and damaging winds during their lifetime in the central and western Midlands.
episodes.209166: Isolated thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a stationary front across upstate South Carolina during the afternoon. One isolated severe storm moved from Anderson County across Laurens County, producing hail up to 2-inch diameter.
episodes.209167: Isolated thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a stationary front across northeast Georgia during the afternoon. One isolated severe storm produced large hail in the Elberton area.
episodes.209304: A stalled front across central Georgia was the focal point for thunderstorm development throughout the day. Scattered strong thunderstorms developed in an area of enhanced CAPE for the time of year and elevated shear. A couple storms were able to produce large hail throughout the day.

A NWS survey team surveyed damage off of Peak Rd in Pomaria in Newberry County where a strong supercell moved through the evening of November 8th, 2025. The survey found multiple large cedar trees that were either snapped or fully uprooted, mainly facing south or southeast in a divergent pattern. There was also extensive siding damage to the north side of a mobile home from wind-driven hail which was up to golf ball sized. The survey along with radar analysis determined that the wind damage was consistent with a strong downburst within the forward flank downdraft of the supercell with winds up to 85 mph.
